description: dbt Labs demo shop: customers, orders and payments (3 CSVs, ~300 rows).
data_notes: Foreign keys do not share the primary-key column name (user_id -> id, order_id -> id).
An order can have several payments, so joining payments to orders multiplies order rows.

questions.question: How many customers do we have?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT count(*) AS customers FROM raw_customers

questions.question: How many orders are there in each status?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT status, count(*) AS orders FROM raw_orders GROUP BY status ORDER BY orders DESC, status

questions.question: What is the total amount paid in dollars, by payment method?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT payment_method, sum(amount) / 100.0 AS total_dollars FROM raw_payments GROUP BY payment_method ORDER BY total_dollars DESC
questions.notes: Unit trap: amount is in cents and must be divided by 100.

questions.question: Who are the top 5 customers by total amount paid?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT c.id, c.first_name, c.last_name, sum(p.amount) / 100.0 AS total_paid FROM raw_customers c JOIN raw_orders o ON o.user_id = c.id JOIN raw_payments p ON p.order_id = o.id GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY total_paid DESC, c.id LIMIT 5
questions.notes: Requires joins through non-obvious keys (user_id, order_id).

questions.question: Show the number of orders per week.
questions.gold_sql: SELECT date_trunc('week', order_date) AS week, count(*) AS orders FROM raw_orders GROUP BY week ORDER BY week

questions.question: How many customers have never placed an order?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT count(*) AS customers_without_orders FROM raw_customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM raw_orders o WHERE o.user_id = c.id)

questions.question: What is the average order value in dollars?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT avg(order_total) AS avg_order_value FROM (SELECT o.id, sum(p.amount) / 100.0 AS order_total FROM raw_orders o JOIN raw_payments p ON p.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.id)
questions.notes: Payments must be summed per order before averaging; averaging payment rows gives the wrong answer. Orders with no payment are excluded.

questions.question: Which orders were paid with more than one payment method?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT order_id, count(DISTINCT payment_method) AS methods FROM raw_payments GROUP BY order_id HAVING count(DISTINCT payment_method) > 1 ORDER BY order_id

questions.question: What share of orders were returned or are pending return?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE status IN ('returned', 'return_pending')) / count(*), 2) AS returned_pct FROM raw_orders

questions.question: And how does that break down by month?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', order_date) AS month, round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE status IN ('returned', 'return_pending')) / count(*), 2) AS returned_pct FROM raw_orders GROUP BY month ORDER BY month
questions.notes: Must reuse the metric from the previous turn.

questions.question: What was our revenue?
questions.notes: Ambiguous: all payments vs. excluding returned orders, and over which period. Assistant should ask or state its assumption.

questions.question: What is the profit margin per product?
questions.notes: There are no product or cost columns; the assistant must say so instead of inventing data.
